forecast.revenue_drivers:
FY2027E: 1H revenue of 177,837mn is booked, so the year is Q3 guidance of $108.0bn (which explicitly assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China) plus a Q4 we hold at roughly +13% sequentially as Vera Rubin enters full production — total ~408,000mn ([R1], [R21]). The first-half base was Data Center $89.0bn in Q2, +117% y/y and +18% sequential on Blackwell Ultra, with ACIE +138% y/y as AI natives, enterprises and sovereigns diversified the customer base ([R9], [R10], [R63]).

FY2028E: we start from management's own ~70% growth guide for fiscal 2028 despite supply constraints, i.e. ~693,600mn ([R6], [R7]). Support comes from $279bn of commitments, mostly memory procurement, secured to meet demand beyond the next several quarters, the PORTS-Pike build (each infrastructure generation ~$150–200bn of NVIDIA revenue under 20-year leases) and over $500bn of third-party compute financing intended to be mobilised with Apollo/BlackRock/Blackstone/Brookfield/Goldman/KKR ([R19], [R18], [R22], [R17]).

FY2029E: growth fades to ~28% (~887,800mn) because we assume hyperscalers internalise more silicon into custom ASICs and because Chinese Data Center compute stays out of the base, partly offset by multi-year site upgrade cycles and the first PORTS-Pike guarantee phase landing in fiscal 2029 ([R48], [R50], [R33], [R18], [R17]).
forecast.margin_drivers:
Gross margin starts from the reported 75.0% in 1H FY2027 and the Q3 guide of 74.0% ±50bp, giving 74.4% for FY2027E; the year-on-year step-up also reflects the absence of the prior-year $4.5bn H20 inventory charge and lower inventory provisions ([R2], [R4], [R26], [R27]). Operating margin of 65.8% uses Q3 GAAP opex of ~$9.2bn and lets opex grow a little faster than revenue into Q4 ([R3]).

FY2028E gross margin eases to 73.5% and operating margin to 64.5% as memory procurement scales with the $279bn commitment book and the mix moves toward full-rack Vera Rubin systems (a 72-GPU rack priced above $7mn) that carry more purchased content per dollar of revenue, while opex builds with the platform transition ([R19], [R49], [R58]). FY2029E takes gross margin to 73.0% and operating margin to 63.5% on continued custom-silicon price competition and cheaper rivals, partly offset by scale ([R48], [R52]).

Other income is held at 1.5%/1.3%/1.2% of revenue — net interest and similar, deliberately excluding the $15.9bn Q1 and $7.8bn Q2 net gains on equity securities, which do not recur ([R25], [R28]). Tax is 15.5% in FY2027E and 16.0% thereafter, near the FY2026 effective 15.1% and allowing for the OBBBA impact in the reconciliation ([R29]).
forecast.vs_consensus:
FY2027E revenue of ~408,000mn (+88.9%) is about 1% below consensus of 411,653mn (+90.6%): the Q3 guide of $108.0bn is only ~12% sequential versus 18% in Q2 and excludes all China Data Center compute, so we do not extrapolate the second-quarter sequential rate into Q4 ([R1], [R9], [R5]). FY2027E EPS is modestly above consensus because we carry the 75.0% first-half gross margin and the 74.0% Q3 guide through the second half rather than assuming further erosion ([R2], [R14]).

FY2028E revenue of ~693,600mn (+70%) is essentially in line with consensus (+68.2%) but rests on management's own ~70% guide, which we take at face value because it is backed by $279bn of commitments, full production of Vera Rubin and the PORTS-Pike/third-party financing structure ([R6], [R7], [R19], [R21], [R18], [R22]).

FY2029E has no consensus reference in our inputs; we fade to +28% on custom ASIC competition and customer concentration, which is the main place our path could sit below a straight extrapolation of the FY2028 ramp ([R48], [R50], [R52]).
forecast.key_risk: The assumption most likely to be wrong is the FY2028 +70% starting point: it requires memory (HBM) and packaging capacity to arrive on the schedule implied by the $279bn commitment book, and requires hyperscalers not to shift budget to in-house ASICs faster than we assume ([R19], [R48], [R50]). Early warning would be the Q3 FY2027 report on 17 November: Q4 guidance below roughly $120bn or Data Center growth flattening sequentially, inventory rising above the $25.8bn second-quarter level without matching revenue, commitments climbing again without a lift in guidance, or any drawdown on the customer financing guarantees (capped at $105bn, first phase in fiscal 2029) ([R61], [R23], [R17], [R37]).
forecast.remainder: The FY2027E revenue forecast implies revenue of 230,070mn for the second half (+83.9% year on year), against +95.8% reported so far this year. Consensus for those quarters (Q3 FY2027E + Q4 FY2027E) is 233,460mn, so our forecast is -1.5% versus the Street for the second half.

The operating evidence favours the bull: Data Center hit a record $89.0bn in Q2 FY2027 and management guides FY2028 revenue growth of about 70% (2 October 2026). The price implies 40.2% growth for five years; our forecast takes the guide, then fades in FY2029 as custom ASICs take share and China compute stays out. Earnings quality is the weak link: cash conversion of 0.86x and net profit lifted by non-recurring equity-securities gains. Scenarios value NVDA at USD 180.43, so Hold stands even though the debate judged the bull case stronger on business evidence; the gap to the brokers' median target is our FY2029 fade and the scenario weights.

Cash conversion of 0.86x and net profit at 101% of operating profit flag earnings quality, not demand.

narrative.company_overview:
NVIDIA designs accelerated-computing platforms: GPUs, networking (InfiniBand, Spectrum-X, NVLink) and full rack-scale systems, reported through two segments, Compute & Networking and Graphics. Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue (193.7bn), with Gaming 7.4%, Professional Visualization 1.5%, Automotive 1.1% and OEM & Other 0.3%. The United States was 69.3% of FY2026 revenue, Taiwan 19.6% and Mainland China & Hong Kong 9.1%.

Customers are hyperscalers, about 50% of Data Center revenue, plus AI clouds, enterprises, sovereign and industrial buyers, a base that broadened in Q2 FY2027. NVIDIA does not fabricate: it depends on third-party foundry, packaging and memory supply, which caps shipments. Its edge is the software ecosystem and a one-year product cadence across Blackwell Ultra and Vera Rubin, which custom ASICs and AMD's Helios rack must erode budget by budget.
narrative.financial_analysis: 1H FY2027 revenue rose 95.8% to USD 177.8bn and the latest quarter alone rose 105.9% to USD 96.2bn; gross margin reached 75.0% from 66.6%, operating profit rose 134.2% and free cash flow rose 76.5% to USD 70.0bn. We forecast FY2027E revenue of USD 407.9bn (+88.9%, about 1% below consensus) and EPS of 9.61 against consensus 9.31, carrying the 74.0% Q3 guide into the second half; FY2028E revenue of USD 693.4bn (+70.0%) follows management's ~70% guide, and FY2029E fades to +28.0% as custom ASICs bite. Over five years operating margin climbed from 37.3% (FY2022) to 60.4% (FY2026) and ROE reached 101.5%; net cash was USD 23.2bn at 26 Jul 2026 while total debt rose to USD 33,366mn from USD 8,468mn, and cash conversion is 0.86x with an accruals ratio of +10.9%.
narrative.valuation_overview: The rating value is the probability-weighted scenarios: bear USD 99.04 (25%), base USD 187.78 (55%) and bull USD 261.95 (20%), giving USD 180.43, 3.3% below the USD 186.64 price. The model's mechanical DCF, on consensus revenue and a 43.3% FCF margin, gives USD 208.05; the bridge's largest step is -17.66, from using our revenue forecast instead of consensus. Peer multiples sit far above — median forward P/E 17.2x against 11.7x, EV/EBITDA 35.7x against 22.2x — while the 38.1x P/E on last-fiscal-year EPS is the 6th percentile of five years. The reverse DCF needs 40.2% growth for five years; 61% of Monte Carlo draws exceed the price, median USD 205.15. Buy needs USD 156.90, Sell USD 200.48.
narrative.competitive_analysis: Against AMD, Broadcom, Marvell and QUALCOMM, NVIDIA's latest-quarter revenue growth of +105.9% compares with a 40.6% peer median, gross margin 74.7% with 54.6% and operating margin 66.2% with 18.9%; its trailing-twelve-month ROE of 117.2% exceeds the 30.4% median, on a different basis from the FY2026 DuPont ROE of 101.5%. It still trades at a discount on trailing and forward earnings and EV/EBITDA, though at 19.7x book versus 8.7x it is the expensive one on assets. The edge is platform breadth — GPU, networking, software orchestration and a one-year cadence — letting it price rack-scale systems rather than chips. The threat is structural: hyperscalers, roughly half of Data Center revenue, are the customers building custom ASICs and renting TPUs.
narrative.news_summary: News has turned negative since the price date. On 9 November 2026 Reuters reported the shares sliding after the board opened an independent probe into whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort; a separate 8 November report alleged a relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, an allegation the company has not confirmed. Mohamed El-Erian argues key-man risk is not adequately priced. Earlier items were mixed: one broker moved to Hold on inventory turnover at a multi-year low of 3.35x, while others cite the enlarged buyback and the record second quarter.
narrative.report_summary: Management guided Q3 FY2027 revenue of $108.0bn ±2% with no China Data Center compute assumed, gross margin of 74.0% ±50bp and GAAP opex of about $9.2bn (26 August 2026), and guided FY2028 revenue growth of about 70% despite supply constraints (29 September and 2 October 2026). Policy: no Data Center Hopper shipments went to China in Q1 FY2027 versus $4.6bn a year earlier. Corporate events: the quarterly dividend rose to $0.25 and buybacks were expanded by $80bn on 18 May 2026, $40bn was repurchased in 1H FY2027, and a further $150bn was authorised on 28 September 2026, taking the programme to $235bn. The 10-Q flags dependence on third-party foundry, packaging and memory supply; the 10-K lists competition, supply and demand mismatches, product defects and geopolitics. An 8-K of 17 August 2026 disclosed a material agreement and new financial obligation.

rebuttals.response: The scenario DCF is one method; the model's mechanical DCF gives USD 208.05 (+11.5%) and 61% of Monte Carlo draws sit above today's price. Broker median target is USD 322.50, and 30 brokers are 100% positive.
Operating profit still grew +134.2% to 117,270 and free cash flow rose 76.5% to 69,987 in 1H FY2027. Excluding equity gains, the operating business is the driver, and net cash is 23,220.

deep.variant_view: Brokers are unanimous — 30 positive ratings and a median target of USD 322.50 (+72.8%), the most cautious USD 275.00 — and every target sits above our USD 180.43. The bridge to the mechanical DCF has three steps: our revenue forecast instead of consensus (-17.66), our base case's FCF margin (-2.61) and the bear and bull cases at their probabilities (-7.35). The largest is the revenue path: we take management's ~70% FY2028 guide, then fade FY2029 to 28.0% as hyperscalers internalise silicon and China compute stays out.

Second, earnings quality — cash conversion stuck near 0.86x while the $279bn commitment book and $105bn guarantees absorb cash. Third, the board probe escalating and distracting management into 17 November.

company.description: NVIDIA Corporation operates as a data center scale AI infrastructure company in the United States, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Europe, and internationally. It operates through Compute & Networking, and Graphics segments. The Compute & Networking segment provides data center accelerated computing and networking platforms and artificial intelligence solutions and software, and automotive platforms and autonomous and electric vehicle solutions, including software. The Graphics segment offers GeForce GPUs for gaming and PCs; Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs for enterprise workstation graphics. The company's products are used in gaming, professional visualization, data center, and automotive markets. It sells its products to original equipment manufacturers, original device manufacturers, system integrators and distributors, independent software vendors, cloud service providers, add-in board manufacturers, distributors, automotive manufacturers and tier-1 automotive suppliers, and other ecosystem participants. It has a collaboration with Cisco to develop Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP), a high-density optical module pluggable transceiver. It has a collaboration with ChipAgents to develop Build-A-Chip-Bench, a benchmark for AI agents carrying chip design tasks and The Company has a strategic alliance with MediaTek to build the next generations of AI computing platforms. NVIDIA Corporation was incorporated in 1993 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.
